context: a letter from Robert Patterson, which you are answering
exchanges:
My dear Sir

I copy for you a note, that I hope may possess some interest. Should you ever think of publishing it, I think it would be only right to the gentleman who is my authority for the fact, to send a copy of the note to him for revision so as to avoid all chance of error.

I am Very truly Yours | Robert Patterson.

Chas. Darwin Esq

PS. Your old friend Ogilby, and Dr. E. P. Wright of Dublin, spent last Tuesday evening in my house.

My dear Sir

I [would] like to thank you for so kindly taking the trouble of communicating the Rat V. Rabbit case. I am very glad to have all such facts, but it is doubtful whether I would require to use it, so I will not give trouble to your informant of inquiring.

With many thanks, pray believe me my dear Sir | Yours sincerely | Ch. Darwin
